context_notes: One recurring defect dominated this milestone and is the thing to carry forward: a control ships GREEN while being bypassable, because every test fixture used the one input spelling the control already handled. It recurred in 26, 27, 27.1, inside 27.2's own fix, and again in 28 (three Criticals). What actually caught it each time was adversarial mutation testing by the reviewer — delete the control, see whether anything reds — not the suite passing. The structural mitigation now in force: author the adversarial-input table BEFORE the fix, run the new test against pre-fix code, and confirm it fails FOR THE STATED REASON. Two execution traps also cost real time: (1) an inverted `! uv run pytest` gate exits 0 on a collection/import error and masquerades as RED — run RED selections plain and read the output, and note that passes reported alongside failures prove collection succeeded; (2) `git commit` publishes the ENTIRE shared index, not just what the preceding `git add` named, so with concurrent executors every commit must be `git commit -- <pathspec>` with `git diff --cached --name-only` inspected first. The milestone's machinery is complete and every gate is green; what remains is genuinely human, and the whole point of Phases 28-29 is that no agent can discharge it.
